business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European) with primacy of directly applicable European Union law, including EU regulations and directives
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — intra-EU freedom of establishment and free movement of capital
More than 90 Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) in force, including the Luxembourg-China BIT and Luxembourg-Singapore BIT
More than 80 Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) in force, including with the United States, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong SAR, the United Kingdom and Singapore
EU Free Trade Agreements applicable through Luxembourg's EU membership, including the EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended following the CJEU judgments in Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq.; EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843 as transposed; EU sanctions regulations applicable via Luxembourg law and treaty practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official extract from the home-country commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country commercial register, company registry or Chamber of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Luxembourg consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of each shareholder, director, authorized signatory and UBO's valid passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country public notary or consular officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record / judicial record extract for each proposed manager and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country criminal records authority or central judicial registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the proposed SARL share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-vault bank or financial institution of each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and, if required by the Luxembourg notary, Hague Apostille or Luxembourg consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ongoing screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized representatives and UBOs against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, FATF public statements and CSSF guidance; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons and family members or known close associates, including a 12-month post-employment monitoring period; because the target payment rails include Airwallex, logistics remittance and cash-on-delivery, the SARL shall also be screened against OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists where USD clearing or correspondent banking is involved; any match or material inconsistency must be resolved before the Luxembourg notary signs the articles of association.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS records company names in the Latin alphabet. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the content of the articles of association must be available in French, German or Luxembourgish as acceptable filing languages. A SARL name must contain or be followed by 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'; the name must not be misleading, contrary to public order or confusingly similar to an existing RCS name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Investment Fund / Fonds d'investissement / SICAV / SICAF / UCITS
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Securities Exchange / Clearing House
Établissement public / Public Establishment / Grand-Ducal / Ministère / Ministry
Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a RCS name refusal, the instructed Luxembourg notary or counsel shall first request a written statement of reasons from the RCS. The applicant may then either submit a modified name through the LBR portal or file a formal administrative appeal to the Luxembourg Minister of Justice within 30 days of notification; an adverse decision may be further appealed to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification of the administrative refusal. If the name is rejected merely on similarity grounds, a conditional name reservation is also available; the notary must retain the final RCS name-clearance evidence in the incorporation file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not strictly prohibited for a Luxembourg SARL and is frequently accepted for administration, provided that a physical address in Luxembourg exists, mail and corporate records are accessible, and any director or registered agent can receive judicial and administrative notifications. However, for a cash-on-delivery e-commerce business using logistics remittance and Airwallex, a pure virtual office with no local management, independent local bank relations or document storage will materially increase VAT and corporate tax-residency risk and will likely be rejected by reputable bank openings and payment-payment providers. Therefore, a virtual office is permissible but not advisable without an additional local administrative service or director.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate — approximately 10-15% within the first 24 months of operation. The RCS, tax administration and AML-regulated bank partners may undertake unannounced visits or remote verification checks, especially if the SARL registers for VAT, applies for cross-border e-commerce payment rail onboarding, or claims intra-community supplies; documentary mass-market COD settlements may also trigger a CSSF-related financial intelligence review.

Notarization of the articles of association of the SARL before a Luxembourg civil-law notary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing and validation with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Apostille and consular legalization of up to three foreign corporate and identity documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced AML/KYC and PEP/sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg AML compliance advisor / instructed law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg corporate service provider / office services provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg counsel legal opinion on incorporation, VAT/e-commerce treatment, AML/CFT compliance and commercial substance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended hourly / fixed-fee market benchmark for a standard SARL formation package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016; complemented by the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) containing the Articles of Association (Statuts), electronically filed with the RCS by the drafting notary; publication of a legal extract in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,000), fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash at incorporation; capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution or an EEA-based bank and is released to the company only upon RCS registration; the notary must certify the deposit and the bank's blocking attestation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company accepts the subscription of its entire issued share capital of EUR 12,000, fully paid in cash, and acknowledges that the paid-up capital is held in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution pending RCS registration. RESOLVED, that the registered office be and is hereby fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the Manager is authorised to execute any lease or administrative arrangement required. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signature authority to represent the company and to complete all statutory filings, including RCS registration, RESA publication, social security enrolment, VAT registration, and the business establishment permit application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS; online reservation via the LBR ePortail / MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative certificate search in the RCS central index and the Luxembourg company name database; file an electronic application for a negative certificate (certificat de non-immatriculation) for the proposed corporate name; the certificate confirms the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, trademark, or commercial name. The notary will rely on this certificate when drafting the articles.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (passport or national ID) of all subscribing shareholders
Proposed corporate name and statement of object
Contact details and nationality/residency declarations of shareholders
Power of attorney (if a representative files on behalf of subscribers, certified copy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a modified name request or submit a written objection with explanatory arguments to LBR; alternatively, secure a waiver/consent from the conflicting rights holder; upon refusal, appeal to the administrative chamber of the Luxembourg administrative court within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notaire) in Luxembourg and the chosen Luxembourg/EEA credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the company 'in formation' and deposit the full EUR 12,000 share capital; obtain the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary. The notary verifies the legality, drafts the Statuts, and conducts the general meeting of incorporators to adopt the articles, approve the share subscription, appoint the initial Manager(s) (Gérant), and fix the registered office address. The notarial deed is signed before the notary by all shareholders or their proxies.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking attestation of the paid-up capital (EUR 12,000)
Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Negative name certificate from LBR
Passports and identity proofs of shareholders
Proof of residential address of shareholders and managers
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each prospective Manager
Consent of the owner of the registered office premises (letter of availability / lease agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary will issue a preliminary title report identifying missing documents or regulatory concerns; correct the documentation or amend the draft articles; if the notary declines to proceed, engage a second notary or seek judicial intervention before the District Court of Luxembourg; re-execute the deed after curing defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); filing performed electronically by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the notarial deed, the request for registration, and the RCS electronic filing form through the LBR secure portal. The RCS verifies the deed's validity, the manager's capacity, the registered office, and the paid-up capital declaration. Upon clearance, the RCS registers the company, allocates the RCS registration number and communicates the legal entity identification data. Legal personality is acquired on the date of RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation (electronically transmitted by the notary)
RCS incorporation filing form (formulaire de dépôt électronique)
Identification data and specimen signatures of Managers
Copy of the bank blocking attestation
Registered office consent/lease
Declaration of the notary of legal compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rejection (annex of omission), the notary or the applicant must cure within fifteen days by submitting the supplementary evidence; resubmit the corrected electronic dossier; if administrative refusal persists, lodge an appeal before the District Court of Luxembourg sitting in commercial matters within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Constitutional Deed in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the deed of incorporation and the RCS registration data to RESA for mandatory publication. RESA publishes a legal extract containing the company's name, registered office, object, capital, managers, and RCS number within one month of registration. Publication triggers full enforceability of statutory provisions against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Notarized deed of incorporation
Legal extract to be published (prepared by the notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA rejects the filing as incomplete, the notary immediately refiles the corrected extract; if the legal effect of publication is challenged, a declaratory judgment from the District Court may be obtained to confirm the publication date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Enrolment and Operational Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce, Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under the duty of legal counsel or the delegated fiduciary, the company must enrol its manager and any employees with the CCSS within eight days of incorporation, register with the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce and Chamber of Employees (registration in the trade chamber registry), apply for a VAT number with AEDT where taxable supplies exceed EUR 35,000 or on voluntary basis, and submit the application for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) to the Ministry of the Economy via the Single Point of Contact (Guichet.lu). No COD-specific financial licence is required, but the firm must implement anti-money laundering (AML) internal controls appropriate to a Medium-Risk cash settlement model.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Proof of identity of the manager(s)
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of applying manager
Diploma or professional experience certificates supporting manager's fitness (for establishment permit)
Lease or deed evidencing registered office
Bank account details (operational account, post-escrow release)
AML/CFT internal control policy declaration (for cash collection)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CCSS/AEDT reject the enrolment for incomplete data, refile after correcting the registrant details; if the establishment permit is refused, submit a reasoned administrative appeal to the Minister of the Economy within three months and, in parallel, regularize the applicable criminal background or qualification issue; interposition of a joint-stock agent is not permitted for the managerial qualification condition.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Small and Medium Enterprises (Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale des PME), represented operationally by the Single Point of Contact (Guichet des autorisations d'établissement, MyGuichet.lu)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) for Mail-Order and E-Commerce Retail Activity with Cash on Delivery Settlement

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), in coordination with the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registered Facility (Établissement classé – Category C): simple registration under Article 2 of the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments for a logistics/warehouse facility below the full EIA threshold (no full Environmental Impact Assessment required where floor area < 10,000 m² and no cold storage or flammable bulk storage); an EIA screening notice is filed with the communal administration alongside the building permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 November 1992 on discharge into municipal sewers (pH 6.5–9.5, BOD ≤ 400 mg/l, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/l, total suspended solids ≤ 500 mg/l); no direct surface water discharge without a prior environmental permit; VOC and solvent emissions: negligible for packaged goods warehouse, but if any repackaging or cleaning operations occur, comply with the VOC emission limit values of the Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing Directive 99/13/EC (solvent consumption threshold < 15 t/yr triggers only record-keeping); waste: mandatory adherence to the national waste management plan under the Law of 21 March 2012, take-back obligation for packaging waste and registration under EPR (Green Dot / Valorlux) for transport packaging.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours – CGDIS): obtain the fire department's approval of the building plans and a post-completion fire safety inspection certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) before operating the warehouse and dispatch areas; structural load clearance via a certified engineering inspection of racking systems (EN 15512 compliance) and for the building's load-bearing capacity; occupational safety clearance from the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines – ITM) including registration of the workplace, preliminary safety audit, first-aid equipment, and ergonomic assessment of packing stations; issuance of the municipal building occupancy permit (certificat de conformité au permis de construire) by the competent Commune for the COD warehouse and office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct tax: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); VAT and registration duties: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Customs: Administration des Douanes et Accises; unified e-portal: MyGuichet.lu; corporate registry: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL is formed by notarial deed registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), which assigns the statutory national identification number (matricule). VAT registration is filed with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu, attaching the RCS extract, articles of association, beneficial-ownership declarations, head-office proof and director identification; the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number (prefix LU + 8 digits). For customs operations the taxpayer must obtain an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration. No local agent is required for a resident SARL, even if wholly foreign-owned.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime; a SARL is an opaque corporate CIT taxpayer resident in Luxembourg, subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income with participation exemption available. Available elections: (i) VAT group registration (assujetti unique, Art. 60 VAT law); (ii) corporate fiscal unity (intégration fiscale, Art. 164bis LIR); (iii) participation exemption claim (Art. 166 LIR); (iv) IP box election (Art. 50ter LIR); (v) ATAD hybrid-mismatch alignment choices (Arts. 168septies et seq. LIR).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / TVA) — EU-harmonised system under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic registration threshold applies: every taxable person carrying on an independent taxable activity must register irrespective of revenue. The optional small-business franchise (Art. 6 VAT law) exempts turnover up to EUR 35,000 for goods and EUR 25,000 for services; export-oriented SARLs commonly waive the exemption to recover input VAT. For Union B2C distance sales (e-commerce), registration via the Union One-Stop-Shop is triggered once EU-wide distance-sales turnover exceeds EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is currently mandated in Luxembourg. B2B/B2C invoices are issued, archived and audited ex post under Arts. 88/90 VAT law and retained for 10 years; B2G e-invoicing uses PEPPOL under Directive 2014/55/EU. VAT returns (monthly/quarterly) and EU recapitulative statements are filed electronically through the AEDT portal; the EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age package is expected to introduce mandatory e-reporting/clearance from approximately 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods consigned to non-EU emerging-market buyers qualify at 0% under Art. 62 VAT law (implementing Art. 146(1) of Directive 2006/112/EC) where the goods leave EU customs territory within three months of supply; cash-on-delivery e-commerce consignments satisfy this condition when carrier and customs records prove physical exit. Intra-Community supplies (Art. 43 VAT law) are also zero-rated subject to the customer's valid VIES-registered VAT ID. International freight, logistics and ancillary services directly connected with exported goods are eligible for the corresponding export-services exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EX-A) lodged with Luxembourg Customs (AES/ECS-confirmed)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment proof evidencing export proceeds receipt
Customer purchase order and COD delivery confirmation issued by the foreign carrier or logistics partner
VIES validation printout of the customer VAT ID for intra-Community zero-rating
EORI and transport booking records retained in the VAT file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT audits export zero-rating strictly on contemporaneous export evidence; missing or internally contradictory documentation causes immediate reassessment of 17% VAT on the sales price plus statutory default interest. Fictitious export declarations trigger the 10-year fraud limitation period, loss of input-VAT deduction, administrative fines under the General Tax Law of 22 May 1931, publication of the decision, and criminal sanctions (fines and imprisonment up to 5 years) for deliberate evasion. Clawbacks are retrospective and are not relieved by the foreign customer's subsequent insolvency.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Central Bank of Luxembourg; banking and AML/CFT supervision is also exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate foreign-exchange administration exists in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible and Luxembourg implements the EU free movement of capital under Articles 63–66 TFEU. Both current and capital account operations are liberalized; there are no exchange-control approvals, surrender requirements, or central-bank permits for profit remittance. Dividend repatriation and distribution of profits are subject to standard withholding tax procedures and ordinary corporate tax filings, but not to any convertibility or liquidity restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg mandates no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no minimum conversion ratio, and no regulatory timeline for repatriation of trade receipts. Cash-on-delivery revenues from emerging-market jurisdictions may be collected and held in foreign currency, or converted freely at market-based rates. For financial reporting and tax purposes, all non-euro transactions must be translated into euro using the ECB or a reliable institutional reference rate at the relevant valuation date.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operating Account
Operating Account with Dedicated Cash Management
Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility
Capital Escrow Account for Initial Share Capital Deposit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for use as a non-bank ancillary payment channel. The legal constraint is that the Luxembourg SARL must maintain its principal settlement account at a Luxembourg- or EU-authorised credit institution; a non-EU electronic money institution cannot passport into Luxembourg without a licensed branch. EU-licensed EMIs/PIs may be used for multi-currency collection, FX conversion, and local payout rails in emerging markets, but the entity must independently satisfy AML/CFT due-diligence and cannot rely exclusively on a third-country EMI as its treasury backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video identification and online KYC may be accepted by Luxembourg banks for low-risk profiles, but a medium-risk cross-border cash-on-delivery business typically triggers mandatory in-person attendance of at least one effective manager or UBO at the bank's Luxembourg office. Original or certified corporate documents, proof of registered office, substance evidence, source-of-funds documentation, and identity verification of signatories are generally required; an in-person interview or visit to a Luxembourg notary may also be imposed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered ownership structure with nominee or non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized incorporation documents, updated share register, Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing proof, UBO declaration, full organisational chart showing individual ownership, and written explanation of any fiduciary or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery settlement flows introducing unverified cash collection agents in emerging markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed logistics and distribution agreements, transaction-level COD settlement statements, monthly reconciliation reports, KYC files on each logistics or remittance partner, and a signed compliance undertaking covering origin of cash, record retention, and suspicious transaction reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital transfers with ambiguous purpose or a mismatch between sending entity and beneficiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution, capital increase notarial deed, shareholders' agreement, loan agreement, bank statement evidencing prior debit from the true source account, and the applicable payment purpose code in the SWIFT remittance information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue exposure to sanctions- or FATF-high-risk jurisdictions through remittance counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening report for all material counterparties, external legal due-diligence opinion, negative-media and AML adverse-event searches, and contractual negative-representations and reporting covenants from the partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg SARL's euro account using a TARGET2/SEPA-compliant credit transfer. Field 50K must identify the true ordering entity, and field 70 should carry the bank-adopted purpose code plainly identifying the transaction as direct investment in equity or intercompany credit, with reference to the capital increase agreement or loan contract. The Luxembourg receiving bank will perform source-of-funds verification against the corporate authorization and UBO documentation; amounts above the applicable statistical threshold may require a BCL statistical declaration, but no prior exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to global logistics providers and merchants shall use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers or SWIFT MT700/MT710 commercial letters of credit issued by the Luxembourg bank through its correspondent network. USD disbursements clear via CHIPS/Fedwire, EUR via TARGET2/SEPA, and emerging-market local-currency payouts via an EU-licensed EMI's local clearing or mobile-money rails after compliant FX conversion. Every outgoing disbursement must be matched against invoices, import/export documentation, and contracts, retained for corporate-tax and transfer-pricing audits, and subjected to EU sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards for eligible emerging-market currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) approved by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustices electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a calendar-year company); must also be filed no later than 1 month after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a Commercial Court order upon third-party motion, with coercive fines up to EUR 2,000 and publication; repeated non-filing can lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 300, impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a taxable period ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 December of the following year; electronic filing is mandatory for corporate taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing can incur a penalty up to 10% of the tax due, default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax, and ex officio assessment (taxation d'office) based on available records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal, ICC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ACD (for assessment) and the competent commune (collector)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Integrated with and due by the same deadline as the corporate income tax return: 31 December of the year following the tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and payment expose the company to penalties up to 10% of the communal tax due, monthly interest, and enforced collection by the communal collector; under-declaration may attract additional fines and interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune, IFF, filed with the corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the corporate income tax return; for calendar-year entities no later than 31 December of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquencies attract default interest at 0.6% per month, late-filing penalties up to 10% of the net wealth tax, and risk of administrative revaluation or official assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Luxembourg Sàrl, an independent statutory audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is mandatory if, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: (a) balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million; (b) net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million; (c) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. The audit obligation may also be triggered by a shareholder request holding 10% of the voting rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP, based on the Law of 19 December 2002 transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts and is permissible on a voluntary basis for unlisted entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not mandate a separate annual UBO re-filing. The RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) requires that beneficial owner information be continuously updated and that any shareholding transfer or indirect change be declared within 1 month of occurrence. As part of year-end procedures, management must reconcile the share register with the RBE data and update the registry to reflect any donations, pledges, or transfers in the past year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate of 17% CIT plus 7% unemployment surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax; standalone CIT effective rate is 18.19%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg IP box grants an 80% exemption on qualifying IP income, producing an approximate 5.1% effective rate. Participation exemption allows an 85% exemption for dividends from qualifying participations and a 100% exemption for capital gains if participation conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 – Declaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités; electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu / eCDF platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May following the relevant tax year; a reasonably justified extension may be requested by the Luxembourg authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification and corporate seat information for the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg RCS number, officially appointed director tax residence details, and postal address of the registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial revenue derived from mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery e-commerce transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross COD sales proceeds must be recorded gross without deduction of logistics fees or payment aggregator commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including procurement, local logistics, marketing, and payment processing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Art. 50bis limitation applies if head office or foreign related-party expenses are allocated to the Luxembourg permanent establishment; must be arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable base and application of loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred in Luxembourg may be deducted; foreign source losses are excluded unless expressly re-characterized by a double-tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of tax incentives, participation exemption, and the IP box exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach schedules showing holding periods, participation percentage, and qualifying IP classification for non-resident parent ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessment of CIT, unemployment surcharge, municipal business tax, and withholding tax obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent should confirm whether dividend distribution is material for the assessment period and verify parent-Subsidiary directive eligibility.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a formal reminder and a potential penalty up to EUR 5,000, plus late payment interest; continued non-filing can result in ex officio assessment, daily surcharges, and directors becoming jointly liable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends distributed by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders; may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% holding, 12-month ownership) or eliminated under a relevant DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Luxembourg Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) in the residence state and submit it to the Luxembourg tax administration together with a dividend relief claim. The withholding agent must apply the reduced rate only after receiving an approved exemption certificate; otherwise the 15% withholding is made and reimbursement may be sought via a tax refund claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose statutory withholding tax on interest or royalties paid to non-resident legal entities; treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and maintains economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required when the Luxembourg group has consolidated group revenue exceeding EUR 750 million; Local File required when related-party transactions exceed EUR 1 million for goods or EUR 500,000 for services, royalties, financing, or intangibles.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulation in the Cayman-style sense, EU ATAD, the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule, and beneficial ownership jurisprudence require genuine economic substance, local decision-making, and business purpose for treaty and directive benefits to apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting cash-on-delivery collections, maintaining dual booking ledgers, or destroying COD transaction records to understate turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax prosecution: amende fiscale equal to 100% of the evaded tax plus tax penalties, interest, and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment of up to 5 years under Luxembourg tax fraud provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations expose themselves to civil restitution of evaded taxes, travel restrictions, and criminal custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominally registered but substantively inactive Luxembourg SARL with no employees, no office, no business function, and no board control solely to conduit payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, antidirector and anti-abuse penalties, reclassification of income within Luxembourg, retroactive reassessment, and withdrawal of tax compliance certifications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil: directors become personally liable for all unpaid corporate taxes, interest, and penalties, and may be prohibited from managing or leaving Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting anonymous cash-on-delivery currency, failing to report suspicious COD collections or related-party remittance flows, or intentionally circumventing Luxembourg AML, Know-Your-Customer, and FATF/AML/CFT obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 1 million for entities and EUR 250,000 for responsible individuals; confiscation of instruments and proceeds; withdrawal of commercial functions and revocation of any relevant licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal prosecution, disqualification orders, asset freezing, travel bans pending investigation, and imprisonment where the breach forms part of organized fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate absence of transfer pricing documentation when related-party COD logistics fees, platform fees, or intra-group financing arrangements exceed prescribed thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty up to EUR 100,000 for non-production of documentation; the Luxembourg tax authorities may estimate taxable income and impose a 20% accuracy-related penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the tax adjustment and penalties where they knowingly caused the absence of contemporaneous documentation or signed inconsistent TP policies.
